items.question: According to the AW169 QRH Approach & Landing procedure (Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.176), at what indicated airspeed is the night-operations landing lights setting for the flying pilot side referenced?
items.explanation: In the Approach & Landing section, the night landing lights step specifies 40 KIAS as the reference speed for the flying pilot side landing light setting.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.176 - Approach & Landing

items.question: According to the AW169 QRH Approach & Landing procedure, what indicated airspeed is associated with the flying pilot side landing light setting for night operations?
items.explanation: The night-operations landing lights step uses 40 KIAS as the reference speed for the flying pilot side.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.176 - Approach & Landing

items.question: According to the AW169 QRH Approach & Landing procedure (AP8.0 p.178), what approach speed is used for the stabilized segment after pre-landing checks and EDCU MISC/AURAL INHIBIT selection?
items.explanation: The Approach & Landing profile calls for a stabilized approach at 70 KIAS after the pre-landing checks and EDCU MISC/AURAL INHIBIT selection.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.178 - Approach & Landing

items.question: Specify the correct value from the QRH: in the AW169 Approach & Landing procedure, which indicated airspeed is given as the target speed for the stabilized approach prior to flare?
items.explanation: The QRH uses 70 KIAS as the target speed for the stabilized approach segment prior to flare.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.178 - Approach & Landing

items.question: At the initial point in the AW169 QRH Approach & Landing profile, what ground speed is specified for establishing the approach?
items.explanation: The Initial point step directs the pilot to establish an approach at 20 kts ground speed, 50 ft above LDP height.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.180 - Approach & Landing

items.question: In the AW169 HVR ROC PAC WIND rate-of-climb performance chart (Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.340), on which helicopter mass are the climb performance values based?
items.explanation: The hover rate-of-climb performance shown in the PAC/WIND chart is based on flight test results at 3200 kg all-up mass.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.340 - HVR ROC PAC WIND

items.question: What all-up mass is assumed for the AW169 hover rate-of-climb performance with PAC and wind as presented in the QRH HVR ROC PAC WIND chart?
items.explanation: The HVR ROC PAC/WIND performance data are referenced to an all-up mass of 3200 kg.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.340 - HVR ROC PAC WIND

items.question: According to the AW169 QRH Contour & H/V Chart A, up to what all-up mass is the flyaway transfer value valid when EAPS is OFF or ON?
items.explanation: Contour & H/V Chart A states that the flyaway transfer value is valid up to 4600 kg all-up mass with EAPS OFF or ON.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.238 - Contour & H/V Chart A

items.question: When consulting the AW169 Contour & H/V Chart A in the QRH, what is the maximum mass covered by the flyaway transfer value with EAPS ON/OFF?
items.explanation: The flyaway transfer value shown in Contour & H/V Chart A is valid up to 4600 kg with EAPS ON or OFF.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.238 - Contour & H/V Chart A

items.question: In the AW169 Taxi T/O CAT A/B performance section (Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.158), at what reference altitude are the engine power checks for Category A/B taxi and take-off based?
items.explanation: The Taxi T/O CAT A/B power check step is referenced to 1000 ft, matching the engine power check tables.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.158 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: According to the AW169 Taxi T/O CAT A/B QRH procedure, which reference altitude should be used when performing the required engine power checks?
items.explanation: Engine power checks in the Taxi T/O CAT A/B procedure are based on a reference altitude of 1000 ft.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.158 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: When setting the pilot's altimeter for the AW169 Category A/B Taxi & Take-Off procedure, which nearest thousand-foot value is used as the standard reference take-off altitude?
items.explanation: The Taxi T/O CAT A/B step 'Pilot Altimeter - Set 0 ft or nearest 1000 ft setting to T/O altitude' uses 1000 ft as the standard thousand-foot reference.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.156 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: The QRH Taxi T/O CAT A/B step 'Pilot Altimeter - Set 0 ft or nearest 1000 ft setting to T/O altitude' implies a standard reference altitude. What is that reference altitude?
items.explanation: The nearest thousand-foot reference used in this context is 1000 ft.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.156 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: In the AW169 QRH Taxi T/O CAT A/B procedure, when completing warnings, cautions and flight-control checks, what reference altitude is associated with this part of the profile?
items.explanation: The later steps of Taxi T/O CAT A/B, including warnings, cautions and flight-control checks, are tied to a reference altitude of 1000 ft.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.160 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: Specify the correct value: what reference altitude is used in the Taxi T/O CAT A/B procedure for the final checks of warnings, cautions and flight controls?
items.explanation: The final checks of warnings, cautions and flight controls in Taxi T/O CAT A/B are referenced to 1000 ft.
references: AW169 QRH Lims-Norm-Perf AP8.0 p.160 - Taxi T/O CAT A/B

items.question: According to the AW169 RFM Engine Power Checks section, what is the main purpose of the Engine Power Assurance Check?
options: To monitor engine health and confirm that available power before take-off is within the limits for using the RFM performance data.
To calibrate cockpit power and torque indicators after maintenance.
To validate that the autopilot and AFCS can follow the performance profiles.
To optimise fuel flow for minimum specific fuel consumption during cruise.
items.explanation: The RFM states that the Engine Power Assurance Check provides a means of monitoring engine health on an ongoing basis and confirming that available power before take-off is within the limits established for the legitimate use of the Rotorcraft Flight Manual performance data.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Engine Power Checks & Hover Power Check Procedure (p.4-10)

items.question: In normal AW169 operations, at what interval is the Engine Power Check required according to the RFM?
items.explanation: Section 4 of the RFM specifies that the Engine Power Check is required every 25 flight hours under normal conditions.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Engine Power Checks (p.4-10)

items.question: Under which condition must the AW169 Engine Power Check be performed daily instead of at the normal 25-hour interval?
options: When either the average ITT margin of the last three samples is less than 10 deg C or the average NG margin is less than 0.2%.
Whenever ambient temperature exceeds ISA + 20 deg C at take-off.
When any single ITT reading exceeds take-off limit by more than 10 deg C.
Whenever the helicopter is operated above 6000 ft pressure altitude.
items.explanation: The RFM states that if the average ITT margin of the last three samples is less than 10 deg C, or the average NG margin is less than 0.2%, the Engine Power Check task must be performed daily.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Engine Power Check Intervals (p.4-10)

items.question: During the AW169 Hover Power Check procedure described in the RFM, which barometric setting must be used on the altimeter?
options: Actual QNH for the departure aerodrome.
QFE for the landing decision point.
Any setting, provided both altimeters agree.
items.explanation: The hover power check procedure directs the crew to set the barometric pressure to 1013 mb or 29.92 inches before carrying out the check.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Power Check Procedure (p.4-10)

items.question: How should the ECS be configured for the AW169 hover engine power check according to the RFM?
options: Set ECS to AUTO with temperature at mid-scale.
items.explanation: The hover power check procedure explicitly requires confirming that the ECS is set to ONLY VENT before performing the check.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Power Check Procedure (p.4-10)

items.question: In the AW169 hover power check, which rotor speed and hover condition are used to obtain the torque value for plotting on the power assurance chart?
options: 103% rotor speed with the helicopter light on wheels or hovering at about 3 ft.
100% rotor speed with the helicopter hovering at 10 ft.
105% rotor speed with skids firmly on the ground.
95% rotor speed in a stationary out-of-ground-effect hover at 30 ft.
items.explanation: The RFM states that with rotor speed at 103%, the pilot sets collective until 'light on wheels' or hover at 3 ft to obtain the torque value used on the figure.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Power Check Procedure (p.4-10)

items.question: In the AW169 hover power check, what does a positive Power Assurance Margin (PAM) indicate?
options: Recorded ITT/NG values are below the maximum allowable, and engine condition is acceptable for flight.
Recorded ITT/NG values are above the maximum allowable, but the helicopter may still be flown within OEI limits.
The aircraft is too light for the test conditions and the check must be repeated at a higher weight.
The power assurance charts are invalid and maintenance action is immediately required.
items.explanation: The RFM explains that if the recorded ITT or NG values are less than the maximum allowable values from the chart, the engine condition is acceptable for flight and the resulting difference (PAM) is positive.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Engine Power Checks (p.4-10)

items.question: What headwind benefit may be credited when operating at the AW169 HOVER CEILING OGE weight in AREA 1 of the envelope?
options: No headwind benefit may be credited.
Up to 25% of the headwind benefit may be credited.
Up to 50% of the headwind benefit may be credited.
Full headwind benefit from the Unfactored Headwind Benefit table may be credited.
items.explanation: The Hover Ceiling OGE section specifies that when operating with HOVER CEILING OGE weight in AREA 1, no headwind benefit is allowed.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Ceiling OGE Unfactored Headwind (p.4-28)

items.question: Unless otherwise authorised by operating regulations, what is the maximum fraction of headwind performance benefit an AW169 pilot may credit from the Unfactored Headwind Benefit table?
items.explanation: The RFM note states that unless otherwise authorised, the pilot is not authorised to credit more than 50 percent of the performance increase resulting from the actual headwind component.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Ceiling OGE Unfactored Headwind (p.4-28)

items.question: In the AW169 OGE hover performance charts, which electrical loads are included for All Engines Operating and One Engine Inoperative conditions?
options: AEO charts at 75% and 25% electrical load; OEI charts at 100% and 75% electrical load on the remaining DC generator.
AEO charts at 100% electrical load only; OEI charts at 50% electrical load only.
AEO charts at 25% electrical load only; OEI charts at 25% electrical load only.
AEO and OEI charts all assume 0% additional electrical load.
items.explanation: The RFM describes AEO OGE hover charts with 75% and 25% generator load options and OEI charts with 100% and 75% load on the remaining DC generator.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Hover Ceiling OGE charts (p.4-28)

items.question: When applying performance corrections after optional kit installation, what minimum OEI climb rate is used in the AW169 RFM for the flyaway manoeuvre?
options: 150 ft/min at Vy with continuous OEI rating.
100 ft/min at Vy with 2.5 min OEI rating.
150 ft/min at Vyse with 2.5 min OEI rating.
300 ft/min at Vy with continuous AEO power.
items.explanation: The Performance Correction After Kit Installation section defines the flyaway minimum OEI climb rate as 150 fpm at Vy with continuous OEI rating.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Performance Correction After Kit Installation (p.4-29)

items.question: How is the Drag Factor determined when several optional kits affecting climb performance are installed on the AW169?
options: By summing the Drag Factors of the individual kits to obtain a combined Drag Factor.
By taking only the highest single Drag Factor among the installed kits.
By averaging the Drag Factors of all installed kits.
By applying a fixed 10% penalty regardless of the number of kits.
items.explanation: The RFM states that if more than one kit is installed, the Drag Factor for the kits must be added together to give the Drag Factor for the combination installed.
references: AW169 RFM Section 4 - Performance Correction After Kit Installation (p.4-29)

items.question: What fuel consumption adjustment does the AW169 RFM require when the Heating System is activated for basic ventilation (outside air temperature up to 20 deg C)?
options: Increase fuel consumption by 2.5% at the same torque.
Decrease fuel consumption by 2.5% at the same torque.
Increase fuel consumption by 5% at the same torque.
No change in fuel consumption is applied.
items.explanation: Section 9 supplemental performance data states that when activating the Heating System (for basic ventilation with outside air temperature up to 20 deg C), fuel consumption must be increased by 2.5% at the same torque.
references: AW169 RFM Section 9 - Performance Correction After Heater Activation (p.9-8)

items.question: According to the AW169 supplemental performance data, how should fuel consumption be adjusted when operating with 75% electrical load instead of the 25% load used in the charts?
options: Increase fuel consumption by 1% at the same torque.
Decrease fuel consumption by 1% at the same torque.
Increase fuel consumption by 5% at the same torque.
No correction is required for electrical load changes.
items.explanation: The note under the heater/ECS performance correction example states that when using 75% electrical load (maximum allowed), fuel consumption is increased by 1% at the same torque.
references: AW169 RFM Section 9 - Supplemental Performance Electrical Load note (p.9-8)

items.question: When using the AW169 range and endurance diagram, how should a headwind be accounted for according to the RFM?
options: Reduce the TAS by the headwind component to obtain ground speed before entering the chart.
Increase TAS by the headwind component before entering the chart.
Ignore wind; the chart already includes a 20 kt headwind margin.
Use indicated airspeed instead of TAS whenever a headwind is present.
items.explanation: The Range and Endurance section explains that the diagram gives still-air range and that to account for wind, TAS should be reduced by the headwind component (ground speed) before entering the chart.
references: AW169 RFM Section 9 - Range and Endurance (p.9-57)
